title: Data in Tables and Single Line Graphs
seo_title: Grade 4 Tables and Line Graphs Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Collect data with time element using appropriate sources; present data in a tabular form, or in a single line graph; interpret data presented in a tabular form, or in a single line graph; solve problems using data for at most two variables in a tabular form, or in a single line graph.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 tables and line graphs worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: data with a time element, reading line graphs, changes over time and two-variable tables. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Time goes across; the values go up.
key_sub: Check the scale before you read a point.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Data with a time element is collected again and again over time: every hour, every day, every month.
  • A single line graph shows how one quantity changes over time. Time goes on the horizontal axis; the values go on the vertical axis.
  • To read a point, go up from the time to the point, then across to the scale. Check what each grid line stands for.
  • A line going up shows an increase, a line going down shows a decrease, and a flat line shows no change. The steepest part shows the biggest change.

Examples

Example

Temperature: 24°C at 8 a.m., 30°C at 12 p.m.

30 − 24

Answer: 6°C warmer

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong grid lineCheck the scale first: each line may be 2, 5 or 10.
Adding instead of subtracting“How much more” asks for a difference.
Using the wrong timeGo straight up from the time you need.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about data?
faq.a: Collect data with a time element, present data in a tabular form or in a single line graph, interpret it, and solve problems using data for at most two variables in a tabular form or in a single line graph.

faq.q: When should I use a line graph?
faq.a: When data changes over time, like temperature every hour.
In Grade 4, yes: start at 0 and use equal steps.
A quantity that changes, like the amount of rice sold.
